dedupe_keys.name: decarbonizing basic chemicals production in north america europe middle east and china a scenario modeling study 2025

description: This case study models decarbonisation pathways for the most energy-intensive part of the chemicals industry, basic chemicals: olefins, aromatics, methanol, ammonia and chlor-alkali, which with the rest of the industry account for about 5% of global greenhouse gas emissions. Instead of a single optimal path, it builds least-cost timelines by modelling abatement projects individually at more than 2,600 production facilities in North America, Europe, the Middle East and China, under scenarios that vary the pace of capital allocation that corporate investors would accept in different future worlds. It was written by Tubagus Aryandi Gunawan, Hongxi Luo, Chris Greig and Eric Larson and posted on arXiv on 10 September 2025. Coverage is the four regions' basic chemicals plants. The paper is available free on arXiv. Findings: in the best environment, deep decarbonisation needs abatement spending above and beyond business-as-usual investment for two to three decades, over 1 trillion dollars cumulatively, while in constrained futures timelines stretch into the second half of the century. Caveats: it is a preprint, and facility data and cost assumptions are not detailed on the abstract page. For simulation it offers facility-level transition scenarios for capacity planning of chemical plants and the energy, hydrogen and carbon capture infrastructure they would need. It is related to the Global Petrochemical Map record in this catalogue. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (arXiv paper).
